title: The Wave Equation

blocks.html: A guitar string, a skipping rope, a drumhead: small vibrations of a stretched string obey the wave equation. It differs from the heat equation by one derivative in time, and that changes decay into oscillation.

$u_{tt} = c^{2}u_{xx}$ on $0 < x < L$, fixed ends $u(0, t) = u(L, t) = 0$, initial shape $u(x, 0) = f(x)$ and velocity $u_t(x, 0) = g(x)$: $$u = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(A_n\cos\frac{n\pi ct}{L} + B_n\sin\frac{n\pi ct}{L}\right)\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L},$$ where $A_n$ are the sine coefficients of $f$ and $B_n\cdot\frac{n\pi c}{L}$ are the sine coefficients of $g$. Mode $n$ has angular frequency $\frac{n\pi c}{L}$ and period $\frac{2L}{nc}$.

A short piece of string with density $\rho$ and tension $\tau$ feels a net vertical force from the tension that is proportional to the string's curvature, $\tau u_{xx}\,\Delta x$; mass times acceleration is $\rho\,\Delta x\,u_{tt}$. So $u_{tt} = c^{2}u_{xx}$ with $c = \sqrt{\tau/\rho}$, the wave speed. Separating, $X'' + \lambda X = 0$ with fixed ends gives $\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}$ as before, but now $T'' + c^{2}\lambda T = 0$ is a simple harmonic oscillator, so each mode vibrates forever with no damping. Two initial conditions are needed, since the time equation is second order: $f$ fixes the $A_n$, and differentiating at $t = 0$ shows $g$ fixes $\frac{n\pi c}{L}B_n$.

blocks.title: Shape and velocity
blocks.q: Solve $u_{tt} = u_{xx}$ on $(0, \pi)$ with fixed ends, $u(x, 0) = -4\sin 3x$, $u_t(x, 0) = -4\sin 4x$.
steps: $c = 1$, $L = \pi$: modes $\sin nx\cos nt$ and $\sin nx\sin nt$.

blocks.title: A guitar string
blocks.q: A string 0.65 m long has wave speed $c = 286$ m/s. What is its lowest frequency in hertz?
blocks.a: 220 Hz (the note A); the overtones are 440, 660, 880, … Hz

blocks.html: With $g = 0$ the solution can also be written as $u$ $= \frac{1}{2}\left(F(x - ct) + F(x + ct)\right)$, where $F$ is the odd periodic extension of $f$ (d'Alembert's formula). It follows from $\sin a\cos b$ $= \frac{1}{2}\left(\sin(a - b) + \sin(a + b)\right)$ and shows the initial shape splitting into two halves that travel in opposite directions at speed $c$.

blocks.name: de-pde
blocks.cap: A plucked string. Play it: the corner splits into two corners that run apart, reflect upside down at the ends, and meet again; after time $\frac{2L}{c} = 2\pi$ the shape repeats exactly.

blocks.name: surface
blocks.cap: Two modes of a string with $c = 1$ as a surface over position $x$ and time (the $y$ axis). Unlike the heat surface, nothing decays: the pattern repeats every $2\pi$.
